subject: Re: SIG questionnaire - encryption & key management artifacts
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acme-telecom.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG questionnaire - encryption & key management artifacts

Hi Neha,

Thanks for taking this. We're working through the SIG questionnaire for our upcoming integration and need a focused set of artifacts around encryption and key management. Can you provide the following evidence or confirm where we can retrieve it?

- HSM attestation (latest attestation cert/report) and statement of compliance
- KDF details used for tenant key derivation (algorithm + test vectors, if possible)
- Envelope encryption description (KEK/DEK separation, wrapping algorithms, MAC)
- Key rotation runbook and an example of a recent rotation (logs, timestamps)
- Transit encryption summary: TLS versions/ciphers, mutual TLS for backend services if used
- Separation-of-duties / access control matrix for KMS/HSM operators

We're aiming to complete SIG by EOD next Thursday; if you can share an initial package or a secure link, that would be ideal. If anything below is sensitive, we can accept redacted copies and a list of available artifacts.

Thanks,
Oliver
Senior Security Manager
Acme Telecom

--
Attachment: SIG_request_v1.pdf (application/pdf - stub)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acme-telecom.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire - encryption & key management artifacts

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to provide a curated package. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we assemble everything:

1) For KDF/test vectors, do you need raw test vectors OR a salted derivation sample from a non-production tenant? We prefer to provide test vectors only (no tenant material).
2) For separation-of-duties, are you looking for a high-level matrix (roles & permissions) or the underlying IAM policy JSONs?

Plan: I will coordinate with ops and cryptography to produce a rotation runbook PDF, the HSM attestation PDF (latest), a KDF spec + test vectors archive, and a small CSV with rotation sample logs. We'll stage them on a secure share with one-time access for your team.

I'll loop in our on-call for HSM evidence and our compliance lead to confirm redaction policy. Target delivery: today EOD PT if our legal review is quick.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

--

Team — forwarding Acme's request (below). Need a small artifact bundle assembled and QA'd. Tasks:

Irene/Laura/Jonas, please drop drafts to the secure share link below and ping me when they're ready for legal/compliance review. If you think anything should be redacted beyond operator IDs (e.g., internal endpoints), flag that.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Hi Oliver — thanks for the patience. We've assembled a curated evidence bundle for Acme Telecom and staged it on a secure, time-limited share. Files included (PDF/ZIP/CSV stubs attached and available on the link):

- rotation_runbook_v1.3.pdf — Key rotation runbook with trigger definitions, rollback procedures, and verification steps. (redactions: operator logins hashed)
- hsm_attestation_2027-03.pdf — Vendor attestation and summary of HSM firmware versions; suitable for SIG/CAIQ review.
- kdf_spec_and_testvectors.zip — KDF algorithm description (HKDF-SHA256), derivation parameters, and synthetic test vectors for verification (no production material).
- rotation_sample_logs.csv — Example of a production rotation cycle (timestamps in UTC, key IDs hashed, event types).
- encryption_transit_summary.txt — Short summary of in-transit protections: TLS 1.2+ accepted, TLS1.3 preferred, list of cipher suites, and note on mutual TLS for internal service-to-service channels.

Secure link (one-time access, expires in 7 days): https://secure-share.redwood.com/s/3f9a2b-kms-evidence
Ticket: SIG-2345

Notes/high level answers to your original bullet list:
- HSM attestation: provided (hsm_attestation_2027-03.pdf).
- KDF/test vectors: algorithm and synthetic vectors provided (kdf_spec_and_testvectors.zip).
- Envelope encryption: described in KDF spec + rotation runbook; KEK/DEK separation uses AES-KW for wrapping and AES-GCM for DEK usage.
- Rotation runbook & sample logs: provided; runbook includes emergency rotation playbook and contact escalation steps.
- Transit: encryption_transit_summary.txt describes TLS posture; we also provide mTLS for inter-service control plane traffic.
- Separation-of-duties: runbook + HSM attestation describe operator roles; for detailed IAM JSONs we can provide a redacted policy dump under an NDA if required.

If you need anything as a native Doc (e.g., redwood-maintained policy JSON) or want us to push artifacts into your Okta-provisioned S3 bucket, let me know and we can coordinate next steps.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
